title: Remote double-free (A,B,A) on an orphaned/pooled page bypasses detection: resolve() releases the page by count==cap without validating the chain, handing a live block back out
scenario: A page whose owning thread has exited is detached to ORPHAN and then QUEUED in a class pool (heap_flush->page_detach->resolve). Its xfree.count is the page's total free count = remote-chain length + folded (local free + unprovisioned). While the page is ORPHAN/QUEUED, remote_free only increments the count and appends to the chain; it never walks it, and the owner's collect()/merge_chain() path never runs. When a cross-thread double free drives the count to exactly cap, remote_free (heap.c:508) sets PENDING and calls resolve(), whose cnt==cap branch (heap.c:380-385) CAS-clears xfree to 0, unlinks from the pool, and calls page_release(r) at heap.c:397 -- WITHOUT the exact-length chain walk that the sibling pool_claim path performs (merge_chain at heap.c:562-563). So the classic free(A); free(B); free(A) pattern (head!=A defeats the immediate-repeat check; count cap+1 is never reached) is accepted, and the page -- which still contains live allocations handed out before the producer exited -- is returned to the page heap and reused. CONFIRMED with orphan_aba.c: a producer thread allocates A,B,L (L live) and exits; the main thread does free(A);free(B);free(A); the allocator does not abort; malloc_usable_size(L) becomes 0 and a subsequent malloc(16) returns L's exact address, overwriting the live block. This bypasses the double-free detection that README and docs/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md section 3 explicitly promise for 'a thread freeing A, B, A remotely'. The existing tests/regress/invalid_frees.c covers only the owned-page variants (bad_aba, bad_remote_then_local with the owner still alive), which are correctly detected; the exited-owner (orphan) case is uncovered. An attacker who can trigger a double free, or a use-after-free write that corrupts a free block's link, on a pool/orphan page thereby turns a detected abort into silent heap corruption / returned-live-memory.
fix: In resolve()'s cnt==cap branch (src/heap.c ~380-385), validate the remote chain before releasing, mirroring pool_claim: after the successful CAS that stores 0 into xfree (and the QUEUED pool_unlink), call merge_chain(r, xf_ptr(x), cnt - r->x.folded); then set give_back = true. merge_chain walks exactly (cnt - folded) nodes, checks each is an in-page block boundary and that the terminator is 0, so A,B,A (a cycle -> length mismatch) and overwritten links abort as 'corrupt remote free chain', while a legitimate full free splices the chain harmlessly onto the local list of a page that is about to be released (cnt == o.prov, so the merge_chain count guard passes). All release routes (remote_free->resolve, page_detach->resolve, pending_drain->resolve) funnel through this branch, so the single change closes every path.
